warning_texts: No deterministic rule checks the label or wording a reader sees for CLM-NET-REVENUE or CLM-REFUND-RATE. The release contract's label_requirements cover only the three country claims, and gate_release_machine records no labels. The blocking gross/net mislabel shows this gap is live, and it stays open

Every semantic agent result in this run (gate0_semantic, the four gate_*_auditor steps and the four worker_* steps) has a placeholder shape. Each summary is 'driver e2e <step>', each created_at is 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z (eight months before this stage was dispatched), and each auditor's evidence/notes
gate_release_auditor returned PASS on one refund-rate check without examining the report text, which is how a mislabelled headline reached the final gate.

audit/check_plan.json lists claims_rendered and caveats_rendered for gate_release_document under accepted_unproven, because their proof run failed with FileNotFoundError. gate0_machine plan_proven nevertheless reports 0 accepted unproven, so these two release-document checks were never shown to fire

metrics/calculated_metrics.json gives net_revenue a numerator field of 40235.02, which is the population's gross sum. It is correct by independent recomputation, but no rule checks it, and a renderer reading that field under the net label would publish gross as net.

The spec period ends on 2025-03-30, while R01, the exclusion reason and the period name 2025-Q1-delivered all call it the reported quarter, and calendar Q1 ends 2025-03-31. That end date looks wrong. It moves net_revenue 35741.52 by 0.00 on this extract only because no row of any status is dated 202

The resolved refund_rate_basis (paying_customers) was applied so that any refund above zero marks a customer as refunded, including partial refunds such as half-refunded orders. That reading drives refund_rate 0.473684 (27/57). On the same 57 customers, counting only fully refunded customers gives 0

The resolved revenue_recognition ruling (net_of_refunds) subtracts every refund recorded on an in-period order row, but the export carries no refund date. The 4493.50 EUR deducted from net_revenue 35741.52 may include refunds issued after the period, and the data cannot confirm or deny this.

The resolved timezone_for_dates ruling (Europe/Warsaw) moves no number: order_date is a plain local date with no time component, and the only out-of-period row (2025-04-01) is a full day outside the window.

All four worker carries are identical boilerplate. Each gives the population definition as status=delivered without the period; the period is carried only in the separate periods field.
